questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A new experience, a break from education at home, weather and culture, and also academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture at the university, history and culture of the area, proximity to city, academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of information and steps necessary to get into the university and to the US. The information was available but there was a lot of information overload. It required a lot of hours

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of emails from the International Office of the host university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of options, but it was expensive. I chose a coop, which was the most affordable option and a good way to meet local students. But the living standards are very different from Copenhagen, as students often share a bedroom. But that is part of the experience:)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: "Off campus" is actually really close to campus in many cases, as long as you choose something close by. Most people live just outside campus. On-campus housing is mostly for college freshmen, who are much younger than Danish students tend to be, so I would choose off-campus housing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very very very expensive. It is an amazing way to meet Americans, but no matter what you do, it is expensive and shared with more people than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was a loooot of work. But worth it

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Motivated application to get into specific campus, a lot of steps, visa application, sign up for classes online - the website was smooth, but it required a lot of time to understand the process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email asking for help, and the website was helpful as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succesful - but some classes are already full when the registration is available for exchange students. But still a lot of options to choose from

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early and set aside some time for the process, because it will take time. But it is definitely worth it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Undergraduate programme is sometimes a lot easier than we are used to in Copenhagen. But it differs from class to class

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was much easier and less theory-heavy. Instead, it requires a lot of active participation throughout the semester. But then, finals are not as heavy work-load

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Much more active participation

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Projecting Power
- Political Discourse in the Twenty-First Century
- UN UNPlugged

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Projecting Power was a good way to learn about political movements in a different geographical area

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general, living costs are very high. Taxes and tips are not included in the first price you see

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food on campus was very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many activities to participate in!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and travel around California. Go to Monterey, San Diego, San Francisco, visit some of the nature parks

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Americans are very open and friendly. Very good opportunities to meet people, both Americans and other exchange students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose a housing option with Americans or join a club

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Different norms when making plans

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Apply for scholarships (legater) and plan to spend a lot of money 
- Be open and ready to meet different people! America is a great place to meet people from many different places
- Make sure to seek new experiences and not only spend time on academics

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am so proud of myself for going far away from home and still managing to get a new routine started. But it has so much to do with the fact that the local students are so open and welcoming, and the fact that the institution is very good at welcoming international students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness, time difference when missing loved ones at home, and living in a house with a lot of noise

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
